body.p: The present application has been reviewed in view of the Final Office Action dated September 16, 2024. Claims 21-23, 25-38, and 40 are pending, with claims 21, 32, and 40 being independent. Claims 1-20, 24, and 39 were previously canceled. Claims 21, 23, 30, 32, 36, and 40 are amended. Applicant respectfully submits that these amendments introduce no new matter. Support for the claim features can be found at least in paragraphs [0016], [0231], [0305], [0306], [0345], and [0393] of the specification as originally filed and FIGS. 33A, 33B, 34, and 35 of the drawings as originally filed.
In view of the following remarks, reconsideration and allowance of this application are respectfully requested.
The Office Action rejected claims 21-23, 25-38, and 40 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement.
Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection and in an effort to advance prosecution, the claims have been amended in a manner believed to overcome the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).
Amended independent claim 21 recites, in part:
determine a sensor glucose value for a blood glucose level in the body of the user based on the peroxide-based output signal and the first and second
oxygen-based output signals; and
wherein the sensor glucose value is determined based on the peroxide- based output signal and the first and second oxygen-based output signals using
the first weight and the second weight, respectively.

MPEP § 2163 states that an objective standard for determining compliance with the written description requirement is "does the description clearly allow persons of ordinary skill in the art to recognize that he or she invented what is claimed." In re Gostelli, 872 F. 2d 1008, 1012, 10 USPQ 2d 1614, 1618 (Fed. Cir. 1989). MPEP § 2163 further states that "to satisfy the written description requirement, an applicant must convey with reasonable clarity to those skilled in the art that, as of the filing date sought, he or she was in possession of the invention, and that the invention, in that context, is whatever is now claimed." "[T]he examiner must set forth express

findings of fact which support the lack of written description conclusion ... [including] providing reasons why a person skilled in the art at the time the application was filed would not have recognized that the inventor was in possession of the invention as claimed in view of the disclosure of the application as filed." (MPEP § 2163.04; emphasis added.) "An applicant shows possession of the claimed invention by describing the claimed invention with all of its limitations using such descriptive means as words, structures, figures, diagrams, and formulas that fully set forth the claimed invention." (MPEP § 2163.02.)

Support for the claim features can be found at least in paragraphs [0016], [0231], [0305], [0306], [0345], and [0393] of the specification as filed and FIGs. 33A, 33B, 34, and 35 of the drawings as filed. Applicant respectfully submits that possession of the claimed subject matter is present in the words, structures, figures, diagrams, and formulas that fully set forth the claimed subject matter.
For example, paragraph [0393] of the specification states:

In an embodiment of the invention, the sensor circuitry supports up to five sensor WORK electrodes (4310) in any combination of peroxide or oxygen sensors, although, in additional embodiments, a larger number of such electrodes may also be accommodated. While the peroxide sensor WORK electrodes source current, the oxygen sensor WORK electrodes sink current. For the instant embodiment, the sensors can be configured in the potentiostat configuration as
shown in FIG. 43.
(Emphasis added.) Applicant respectfully submits that up to five sensors includes three sensors in any combination, so that means, for example:
Peroxide Peroxide Peroxide Peroxide Peroxide Oxygen Peroxide Oxygen Oxygen Oxygen Oxygen Oxygen

Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claim 21 recites a first and second oxygen-based sensor and a peroxide-based sensor, and this is one of the combinations provided by this statement of any combination of peroxide and oxygen up to five sensor WEs. Thus, the specification conveys with reasonable clarity to those skilled in the art that Applicant was in possession of "determine a sensor glucose value for a blood glucose level in the body of the user based on the peroxide-based output signal and the first and second oxygen-based output signals" based on the description contained in at least the above-quoted paragraphs.
Paragraphs [0305] and [0306] of the specification state:
having more than 2 working electrodes.
(Emphasis added.) Applicant respectfully submits that it would be clear to one of ordinary skill in
the art that the features are not limited to just fusing two working electrode (WE) signals, it could
be any value n. Taken together with paragraph [0306], it would be clear to one of ordinary skill in
the art that any combination of oxygen and peroxide for up to five working electrodes/sensors are
supported by the specification as originally filed.
Paragraph [0345] of the specification states:

Embodiments of the invention are also directed to an Analog Front End Integrated Circuit (AFE IC), which is a custom Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) that provides the necessary analog electronics to: (i) support multiple potentiostats and interface with multi-terminal glucose sensors based on either Oxygen or Peroxide; (ii) interface with a microcontroller so as to form a micropower sensor system; and (iii) implement EIS diagnostics, fusion algorithms, and other EIS-based processes based on measurement of EIS-based parameters. More specifically, the ASIC incorporates diagnostic capability to measure the real and imaginary impedance parameters of the sensor over a wide range of frequencies, as well as digital interface circuitry to enable bidirectional

communication with a microprocessor chip. Moreover, the ASIC includes power control circuitry that enables operation at very low standby and operating power, and a real-time clock and a crystal oscillator so that an external microprocessor's
power can be turned off.
Paragraph [0231] of the specification states that:

Within the context of electrode redundancy and EIS, a fusion algorithm may be used to take the diagnostic information provided by EIS for each redundant electrode and assess the reliability of each electrode independently.

that Applicant was in possession of "wherein the sensor glucose value is determined based on the
peroxide-based output signal and the first and second oxygen-based output signals using the first
weight and the second weight, respectively," as recited in independent claim 21, based at least on
the description in the above (and below) quoted paragraphs.
Paragraph [0345] of the specification states:

Embodiments of the invention are also directed to an Analog Front End Integrated Circuit (AFE IC), which is a custom Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) that provides the necessary analog electronics to: (i) support multiple potentiostats and interface with multi-terminal glucose sensors based on either Oxygen or Peroxide; (ii) interface with a microcontroller so as to form a micropower sensor system; and (iii) implement EIS diagnostics, fusion algorithms, and other EIS-based processes based on measurement of EIS-based parameters. More specifically, the ASIC incorporates diagnostic capability to measure the real and imaginary impedance parameters of the sensor over a wide range of frequencies, as well as digital interface circuitry to enable bidirectional communication with a microprocessor chip. Moreover, the ASIC includes power control circuitry that enables operation at very low standby and operating power, and a real-time clock and a crystal oscillator so that an external microprocessor's
power can be turned off.
(Emphasis added.) Also, paragraph [0016] of the specification states:

In yet another embodiment of the invention, a method of performing diagnostics on a subcutaneous or implanted sensor having at least one working electrode comprises defining a vector containing values associated with one or more electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based parameters and values associated with one or more non-EIS-based parameters; defining a respective threshold value for each of the EIS-based parameters and each of the non-EIS-based parameters; performing a first EIS procedure to generate a first set of data for the values associated with the one or more EIS-based parameters; after a calculated time interval, performing a second EIS procedure to generate a second set of data for the values associated with the one or more EIS-based parameters; updating the vector with the first and second sets of data; and monitoring the vector values to determine whether the sensor has lost sensitivity.

(Emphasis added.) In view of the foregoing, Applicant submits that the claimed subject matter with all of its limitations is described in Applicant's specification using such descriptive means as words, structures, figures, diagrams, and formulas that fully set forth the claimed subject matter. (See MPEP § 2163.02.)
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) be withdrawn.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all claims presently pending in the application are in condition for allowance.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Amendment is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action is not explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
